# Artifact Keeper 1.11.13

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 12 changelog entries from 12 pull requests since 1.11.12, all landed on `main` first and brought to the line in #5401, #5445, #5506, #5507, #5508, #5524, #5532, #5558, #5575, #5589, #5592 and #5596 (#5596 fixes a flaky test and ships nothing). Most of it hardens the proxy under load: **a client that gives up on a cold fetch no longer cancels it**, so the cache still fills and the retry gets it (#5220), **proxy load can no longer exhaust the main database pool** (#5475), **an anonymous pull during a database outage gets a retryable `503` instead of a fatal `401`** (#5476), and **a proxied path held under a Package Age Policy can be released as soon as its `409` is sent** (#5223). **The published backend image now uses jemalloc**, so memory no longer grows with each burst of proxy downloads until the container is OOM-killed (#5130). **Scans with long version strings are stored instead of losing every finding** (#5534). On security, **the bundled `grype` and `buildctl` in the backend image and `trivy` in the scanner adapter move to fixed Go dependencies**, so every image published from the line scans at zero HIGH and zero CRITICAL findings (#5565, #5571), and `cargo audit` now ignores RUSTSEC-2026-0459, an advisory on a SQLite crate that no build compiles (#5555). **One schema migration**: migration 339 changes six `scan_findings` columns to `TEXT`, and the line moves from migration 330 to 339. There are new proxy settings, all with defaults, and the scanner adapter moves to 1.5.3.

## Security

- **The backend image's bundled `grype` moves to v0.121.3 and its bundled `buildctl` is rebuilt with `golang.org/x/net` v0.62.0** (#5565, in #5589). A scan of 1.11.12 found no HIGH or CRITICAL issue in the UBI OS packages; every one it reported came from these two Go binaries: GO-2026-6888 (CRITICAL, brotli), GO-2026-6865 (HIGH, klauspost/compress) and the `github.com/docker/docker` findings in `grype`, and CVE-2026-78661 (HIGH, `x/net`) in `buildctl`. grype v0.121.3 no longer depends on `github.com/docker/docker`, so its five `.trivyignore` suppressions are tombstoned. `grype` still reads the v6 vulnerability database, and `buildctl` stays v0.33.1.
- **The scanner adapter's bundled `trivy` is rebuilt with `golang.org/x/net` v0.62.0, and the adapter is published as 1.5.3** (#5571, in #5592). This clears CVE-2026-78661 (HIGH, denial of service in `golang.org/x/net/html`) from `usr/local/bin/trivy`, the third binary it was reported against. The adapter now builds from `ghcr.io/artifact-keeper/trivy:0.76.0-r4`, the unchanged Trivy v0.76.0 source with the `x/net` override, so it still reports Trivy 0.76.0 and a self-run Trivy server stays on 0.76.0.
- **`cargo audit` ignores RUSTSEC-2026-0459** (#5555, in #5558). The advisory is against `libsqlite3-sys` 0.30.1, which is in `Cargo.lock` only because sqlx names its never-enabled SQLite driver through weak features. The backend builds only the PostgreSQL driver, so no SQLite code is in the binary or the images, and nothing an operator runs is affected. sqlx 0.9.0 caps the crate below the fixed 0.39, so `.cargo/audit.toml` carries the ignore until that changes.

## What changed

- **Proxy fetches that a client abandons.** A cold buffered fetch now runs on its own task, so a client that times out and disconnects (yarn after 60 seconds, for example) no longer cancels it: the cache still fills and a retry joins the running fill or reads what it wrote (#5220, in #5401). A request dropped before it is answered now logs `Request cancelled` at WARN with the fields of `Request completed`. The upstream client's timeouts are now settings, it has a deadline on a whole buffered fetch, and it sends HTTP/2 keep-alive PINGs, so a stalled connection is replaced instead of reused.
- **Proxy under load.** The inline download recorder and the cross-replica advisory locks no longer take database connections without a ceiling, so proxy load cannot exhaust the main pool (#5475, in #5508). An anonymous pull whose repository lookup hits a database outage answers `503` with `Retry-After` instead of a `401` that Bazel and cargo treat as fatal; a missing or private repository still gets the same `401` (#5476, in #5507). A fail-closed `423` for an inconclusive scan now logs which of `NoScanner`, `ScanFailed` or `BudgetExceeded` caused it (#5473, in #5506).
- **Package Age Policy holds.** A proxied download refused with `409` under a hold can be released straight away, instead of answering `404 No cached artifact at that path` until the background fetch finished (#5223, in #5445).
- **Memory.** The published backend image and the Linux release tarballs are built with jemalloc, which returns freed memory instead of holding it in glibc's per-thread arenas; a proxy-only mirror that grew from 77 MiB to 3.9 GiB under bursts of Maven downloads no longer does (#5130, in #5524). See `docs/operations/backend-memory-allocator.md`.
- **Scanning.** A scan whose findings carry a version, fixed-version or source string over 100 characters is stored instead of failing with `value too long for type character varying(100)` and dropping every finding. A finding that still cannot be stored now fails only its own scan, and the artifact's other scanners still run (#5534, in #5575).
- **Authentication.** A Basic credential whose password has a multibyte character across byte 8 gets a `401` instead of a dropped connection (#5525, in #5532).

## Upgrade notes

**Migration 339** (`339_scan_findings_text_columns.sql`, the same file as on `main`, so the migration ledger stays consistent with 1.12) changes `scan_findings.affected_version`, `fixed_version`, `source`, `affected_component`, `title` and `source_url` to `TEXT`. On PostgreSQL 16 and later this is a catalog-only change, with no table rewrite or index rebuild, but it takes a brief exclusive lock on `scan_findings`, waiting at most 5 seconds per attempt and retrying.

- If every lock attempt times out (about 35 seconds, for example behind a long-running transaction on `scan_findings`), the migration fails and the server exits at startup. Nothing is left half-applied, and the next start retries it.
- During a rolling upgrade, a replica still on 1.11.12 whose pooled connection prepared a findings query before the migration answers `cached plan must not change result type` on every later run of it, so the findings list, policy evaluation and SBOM reads on that replica can fail until it is replaced or its pooled connections recycle (up to 30 minutes). Replace the old replicas promptly, or upgrade them all at once.

New settings, all optional:

- `PROXY_UPSTREAM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 10; it was a fixed 60), `PROXY_UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 60, unchanged) and `PROXY_UPSTREAM_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS` (default 600, new). A buffered object that cannot be fetched within the deadline (128 MiB at under about 220 KB/s) is no longer cached; raise it for slow upstreams. Streamed downloads are not bounded by it.
- `PROXY_UPSTREAM_MAX_DETACHED_FILLS` (default 16) caps the fills that run detached from their request per replica; past it a fill runs in its request as before, and `0` keeps every fill in its request.
- `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_LOCK_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (default `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_MAX_LOCK_WAITERS` + 1) caps the connections the cross-replica locks hold outside the pool; past it a replica falls back to per-process single-flight.

Behaviours operators may notice:

- Under heavy proxy load, the download count of a serve is skipped once the inline recorder is at its ceiling. The bytes are still served.
- A request that waits out another request's fill now gets a `502`, or the stale cached copy when there is one, instead of a `500`.
- A source build that should match the published image needs `cargo build --release --features jemalloc`; a glibc build that cannot switch can set `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` instead.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.13]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.13/CHANGELOG.md).
